title: Webel
scope: The web department: B2C app, B2B platform, internal dashboard, SEO, email, and the shared component library.
summary: Home-services marketplace. I am responsible for the web department: the B2C app, B2B platform, internal dashboard, SEO, email, and the shared component library.
problemLine: Three web applications with different users, each from a different era of the product and with little in common.
context: Webel connects people who need a service at home with the professionals who provide it. That operation runs through three applications with different users and different rhythms — customers, professionals, and the internal team — plus the SEO surface and the emails around them. Each one came from a different era of the product and shared very little with the others.
audience: Customers booking a service, professionals and companies delivering it, and the internal team running the marketplace.

responsibility.summary: I am responsible for the web department. I decide the architecture, still write implementation code, and maintain what reaches production. Product defines the requirements; I make the technical calls.

fronts.title: The three applications
fronts.description: The B2C app is used by thousands of people a day. The B2B platform lets companies manage teams, services, calendars, leads, chat, service areas, tax details, and payouts. The internal dashboard completes the marketplace operation.

fronts.title: One stack
fronts.description: I migrated the B2C marketplace from Angular to React, extracted the design system into a component library that B2C, B2B, and the dashboard now consume, moved email development to React Email, and built the SEO surface in Astro.

fronts.title: Working with agents
fronts.description: I write the specifications and skills the agents work from, and keep the design-system documentation current so I can review what they produce. The code, the tests, and the final call are mine.

inventory: DAC7 flows, claims handling, and lead capture.
Responsive redesigns of applications that only worked on desktop.
responsibility.teamBoundary: Product sets and prioritises the requirements. I get involved in scope and propose simpler alternatives when I see one, but the product call is not mine. I work the UI through with Design. Inside web, I review another developer's work and pull requests.

decisions.title: Settle on React across the stack
decisions.situation: The B2C marketplace ran on Angular while the rest of web was already React. Every new convention had to be decided twice, and the older codebase got touched as little as possible.
decisions.decision: Migrate the marketplace to React instead of keeping two platforms alive in parallel.
decisions.rationale: The migration had a bounded, estimable cost. Carrying two frameworks got more expensive with every feature.
decisions.change: The main applications share a language and conventions. We stopped repeating the same work in Angular and React, and the existing applications became easier to maintain.

decisions.title: Pull the design system into a shared library
decisions.situation: B2C, B2B, and the dashboard each carried their own slightly different buttons, forms, and tables.
decisions.decision: Extract the UI foundations into our own component library and consume it from all three products.
decisions.rationale: An accessibility fix or a brand change should happen once, not three times.
decisions.change: All three products start from the same components. Brand, accessibility, and behaviour changes happen once, with fewer inconsistencies and repeated edits.

decisions.title: Build SEO in Astro rather than React
decisions.situation: The SEO surface is content: many generated pages, very little interaction. Building it in the same React as everything else was the convenient option.
decisions.decision: Build it in Astro, with static HTML and structured data.
decisions.rationale: On content pages, shipping a React runtime to the browser is cost with nothing in return. Astro serves HTML and only hydrates what needs it.
decisions.change: Content pages load as static HTML with less JavaScript and can ship independently of the applications.

results.statement: Consolidating Angular and React removed duplicate work and made the existing applications easier to maintain.
results.evidence: B2C and B2B now share React, conventions, and review tooling.

results.statement: The shared library reduced inconsistencies and repeated changes across B2C, B2B, and the dashboard.
results.evidence: All three products now consume the same base components.

results.statement: Astro improved content-page performance and let us publish those pages without touching the applications.
results.evidence: Static HTML, structured data, and JavaScript only where interaction needs it.

results.statement: The agent workflow increased delivery frequency while reducing errors and rework.
results.evidence: Each task starts from a specification, context, and reusable skills, then goes through tests and a review of both code and output.

confidentialityNote: SEO template counts, email volumes, and total user numbers are internal and are not published here.
contribution: Responsibility for the web department: implementation, architecture, delivery, and maintenance across three applications.
proof: One shared library replaced three separate implementations of the same components.
The B2B platform covers teams, services, calendars, leads, chat, tax details, and payouts.
The agent workflow increased delivery frequency while reducing errors and rework.
